conviction_note: Nothing decisive is unpriced: the plan (OP 5,200) already trails IFIS (ordinary 6,400 vs 6,100) and the company held its plan at last year's Q3 although 9M OP was already 102% of it. The small positives (FX assumed at 145 against ~157-160, progressive dividend, a revision that is possible but not this company's habit) roughly offset the small negatives (Okayama leak costs still to be quantified, weak fine chemicals in a quarter that runs on fine chemicals). The stock sold its last two beats (-4.7% and -4.4%) and the margin long is crowded (信用倍率 22.6), so p_up 48 on abs 3.3 gives -0.13. impact_sum is +0.25. The two numbers differ in sign but are both near zero; the gap comes from the reaction function and the margin overhang being in p_up and not in any finding.

No options and no skew. priced_lean_pct -0.84 (margin overhang -0.68, run-up -0.17). Run-up +3.3% over 20d and +5.2% over 5d. The company buyback is a steady bid: 705,600 shares / 1.37bn yen of the 2.0bn yen authorisation bought by 2026-09-30, and 188,200 shares in September alone (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261005/140120261005545649.pdf).

findings.finding: The FY plan assumes USD/JPY 145 while the yen sat around 157-162 through the fiscal year. H1 OP of 4,184m is already 80.5% of the 5,200m FY plan, against 74-75% of the final outcome at H1 in FY2024/25. The implied H2 OP of 1,016m is 19% below last year's 1,256m, so the plan has visible room for an upward revision at this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At the Q3 FY2025 print (2025-10-10, 15:30) 9M OP was 4,846m against a 4,750m plan, and the company did NOT revise earnings. It raised only the dividend (75th-anniversary +6 yen), and the stock rose +1.07% to the next close. In Jan 2026 a raised long-term target plus a dividend hike drew +10.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: IFIS already sits above plan (ordinary 6,400 vs 6,100), so a plain hold disappoints nobody. A raise would add a number the street has not seen, but this company's own Q3 habit is to hold. The finding is therefore small. If the market expected a raise, the stock would trade above its July high (2,137) rather than at 1,960.
findings.independence: H1 progress comes from the H1 短信 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260710/140120260708589616.pdf) and the no-revision precedent from the FY2025 Q3 短信 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251010/140120251001566940.pdf). The FX actuals are Yahoo JPY=X monthly closes. These are different documents, but all are public.

findings.finding: The benzene/toluene/xylene wastewater leak at the Okayama plant (found 2026-07-14) stopped synthesis plants 6 and 7, required groundwater pumping and the sealing of an outfall, and left 抜本的な流出防止策 still under study. The company twice wrote that the earnings impact would be disclosed 判明次第, and Q3 (Jun-Aug) is the first period to carry those costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior incident print for this name. On the 2026-07-21 first-report disclosure the stock rose from 1,928 (7/17) to 1,988 (7/21), so the market looked through the incident itself.
findings.why_not_priced: The incident is public but the cost has never been quantified. If the cost were priced, the stock would have reacted to the July disclosures, and it did not. Most of the cost likely sits below operating income as a special loss with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction of the same money as operating profit.
findings.independence: The first report (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260721/140120260720596326.pdf) comes from the same issuer and says the same thing. No third-party source could be reached: the Okayama prefecture page returned 'Request Rejected'.

findings.finding: Fine chemicals OP fell 22.6% in H1 (Q1 -26.3%, Q2 about -20%) on customer demand shifts in pharma/agro intermediates and electronics (generative-AI photoresist) inventory adjustment. In FY2025, Q3 group OP of 1,189m was carried almost entirely by fine chemicals (~1,243m), with agro slightly negative, so Q3 FY2026 likely prints a YoY OP decline. The July Okayama stoppage adds a small production loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock sold off after the Q1 (-4.69%) and H1 (-4.42%) prints, both of which had fine-chem declines alongside agro beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the IFIS Q3 bar of 1,020m already assumes about -14% YoY, and the plan implies about 950m. What remains is a likely 減益 headline on a fine-chem-heavy quarter, which is worth something only to a crowded margin long that reads headlines.
findings.independence: The segment split is from the FY2025 Q3 supplement (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251010/140120251008569988.pdf) and the H1 短信. It shares the Okayama documents with finding 2 only for the minor production-loss point.

findings.finding: Peer Kumiai Chemical reported on 2026-09-11 that its domestic agrochemical sales 大きく伸長 over Nov 2025-Jul 2026, so Japanese farm demand stayed strong into the summer pest season. Hokko's agro is mostly domestic rice and horticulture.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The agro beat at H1 (segment OP +56%) was sold (-4.42%).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer proxy and Hokko itself flagged 前倒し受注 (pulled-forward orders) in H1, which argues for a Q3 payback, so the finding is small. Kumiai fell on its own write-down, which says nothing about Hokko's domestic business.
findings.independence: Kumiai Q3 commentary via a search snippet (Shared Research https://sharedresearch.jp/ja/companies/4996/report/6a8d52420a8ea1f1e2f845c2). The domestic-growth statement in the revision notice itself refers only to 農薬及び農業関連事業 sales rising.

findings.finding: The company runs a 累進配当 policy with FY2026 DPS of 54 yen at a 31.2% payout on 4,460m net, and H1 net of 3,380m is already 76% of that plan. Last year it used the Q3 print to raise the dividend (+6 yen), so a dividend increase at this print is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY2025 dividend raise: +1.07%. FY print with an 8-yen hike plus raised long-term targets: +10.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference: last year's raise was a one-time anniversary payment, and the policy normally resets the dividend at the FY print. If a raise were expected, the 5-day run-in (+5.2%) would be larger than its realised volatility. It is roughly within it.
findings.independence: The policy is stated in the 2026-01-13 capital-cost update (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260113/140120260109531940.pdf) and the payout in the Q1 supplement. Both are company documents.

outside_window.finding: The group reorganisation (merger of 美瑛白土工業, transfer of 北興産業's business into the parent) takes effect 2026-12-01. It brings efficiency gains and is immaterial to this print.
The remaining ~630m yen of the 2bn yen buyback will likely be exhausted by early 2027, so a renewal or a treasury-share cancellation, as in Oct 2025, could follow at the FY print in January.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: possible but against this company's habit (held at Q3 FY2025 with 9M OP at 102% of plan); the plan already sits below IFIS, so a hold is neutral. Returns: buyback already running (68% used); a dividend raise is possible after last year's Q3 precedent. New-year guide: none (Q3). Quarter vs own 進捗率: 9M OP has run at 98.4-98.6% of FY actual in FY2024/25, so FY ≈ 9M + ~70m and Q3 OP decides whether the plan is beaten. My estimate is ~1,000-1,100m against 1,020m IFIS and ~950m implied by the plan.

baseline_tension: Roughly in line with the baseline's mild negative lean (-0.84, mostly margin overhang): my findings net slightly positive (+0.25) and my scaled number slightly negative (-0.13). The strongest positive the release could carry is an upward FY revision or a dividend raise. I looked for both, and the record says this company held its plan at last year's Q3 and raised the dividend only for an anniversary. The +5.2% 5-day run-in was not sized as a negative.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a public series): the fine-chem weakness finding rests on the public H1/Q1 segment trend, so it went from -0.30 to -0.15 and p_up from 47 to 48

Rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): checked. Two of five findings are negative, and baseline_tension names the strongest positive (a revision or dividend raise) and says I looked for it. No further change
Open question 4 (five-day run-in): the +5.2% 5d run-in was deliberately not sized as a negative. Nothing changed
The Okayama finding stays at -0.30 because the release adds a number not yet public (the cost quantification), which rule 1 exempts
